explanation.text: An AI model like Claude is a program that reads text and writes text back. The text you send is the **prompt**. The text that comes back is the **reply**. Python can build prompts, send them, and use the replies.
This module works fully offline. You will learn the Python side first, with a fake AI, so it costs nothing. In lesson 5 you will see how to call a real one on your own PC.
A prompt is a string. Everything you know about strings works here: f-strings, `join`, `strip`, `split`.

explanation.code:
task = "Summarize this in one sentence."
text = "Python is a popular language for beginners."
prompt = f"{task}\n\nText:\n{text}"
print(prompt)

explanation.text: **Tokens.** A model reads text in small pieces called tokens. A token is often a short word or part of a word. A long prompt has more tokens. With a paid service, more tokens means more cost and a slower answer.
Good prompts are clear and specific. Say the task, give the text, and say how you want the answer. Python helps because it builds the same prompt the same way every time.

examples.title: Build a prompt with an f-string
examples.code:
task = "Fix the spelling in this text."
text = "I lik pythn"
print(f"{task}

Text:
{text}")

examples.title: A longer prompt with triple quotes
examples.code:
topic = "loops"
prompt = f"""You are a kind Python teacher.
Explain {topic} to a 12 year old.
Use at most 3 sentences."""
print(prompt)

examples.title: How long is the prompt?
examples.code:
prompt = "Explain what a list is in Python."
print("Characters:", len(prompt))
print("Words:", len(prompt.split()))

exercises.prompt:
Write a function `build_prompt(task, text)` that returns the task, a blank line, the word `Text:`, a new line, and the text.

For example `build_prompt("Summarize this.", "Hi")` gives:

```
Summarize this.

Text:
Hi
```
hints: Use an f-string and `\n` for a new line.

exercises.prompt: Long prompts cost more. Write a function `short_enough(prompt, max_words)` that returns `True` when the prompt has `max_words` words or fewer, and `False` when it has more.
exercises.solution:
def short_enough(prompt, max_words):
    return len(prompt.split()) <= max_words

quiz.question: In AI work, what is a "prompt"?
options: The text you send to the model
quiz.explanation: The prompt is the text you send. The text that comes back is the reply.

quiz.question: What is a token?
options: A small piece of text the model reads
quiz.explanation: Models read text in small pieces called tokens, often short words or parts of words.

quiz.question: Why build prompts with Python code?
options: You get the same prompt shape every time
Prompts must be written in Python
It is the only way to send text
quiz.explanation: A function builds the same prompt in the same way each time, so your results are steadier.
